themes_detail.label: Electrical Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints surged to 14 this week versus a baseline average of 5.1 per week—a 173% spike (z-score: 3.75)—suggesting a potential grid or service issue affecting Park Slope/Carroll Gardens residents this week.
evidence: 14 electrical complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 5.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
173% spike above baseline with z-score of 3.75 (statistically significant)
Timing suggests acute, localized grid or ConEd service failure rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Interview Con Edison about outages or maintenance work in CD 306 this week
Canvas affected residents on Prospect Park West, Seventh Avenue, or other heavily residential blocks for outage details and duration
Cross-reference with power restoration records to identify specific neighborhoods within district hit hardest

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints specifically tied to parks jumped to 4 this week from a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 967% spike (z-score: 7.49)—indicating a new or unusual park activity disruption in CD 306 this week.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
967% spike with z-score of 7.49 (highly statistically significant)
Likely concentrated in Prospect Park or smaller neighborhood parks given district geography
reporting_angles: Identify which park(s) generated complaints—Prospect Park, Washington-Carroll Park, or others
Interview NYC Parks about permitted events, concerts, or maintenance work this week
Speak with nearby residents about timing, source, and impact of noise (early morning construction, music events, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Curb and Sidewalk Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints surged to 21 this week from a baseline of 6.5 per week—a 223% spike (z-score: 3.68)—suggesting accelerated street infrastructure decay in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens this week.
evidence: 21 curb condition complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 6.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
223% spike above baseline with z-score of 3.68
Likely triggered by winter weather, freeze-thaw cycles, or heavy vehicle traffic on specific corridors
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify which streets (Flatbush, Prospect Park West, Seventh Ave) are most affected
Interview NYC DOT about maintenance schedules and whether resource allocation matches complaint volume
Photograph damaged curbs and sidewalks; interview residents and business owners about safety risks (tripping, wheelchair access, stroller hazards)

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints exploded to 3 two weeks ago from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting either new, unregulated street vending or enforcement action targeting vendors in the district.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
2300% spike with z-score of 8.69 (extremely statistically significant)
Vendor Enforcement complaints also spiked 540% last week (4 vs. 0.6 baseline), suggesting coordinated city action or new vendor proliferation
reporting_angles: Interview Department of Health or NYC Business Integrity Commission about enforcement blitzes in Park Slope last 2 weeks
Identify which neighborhoods (Carroll Gardens waterfront, Prospect Park perimeter, Flatbush corridor) saw vendor activity
Speak with vendors and residents: Are unlicensed vendors exploiting new opportunities, or is the city cracking down on existing operations?

themes_detail.label: Commercial Waste & Maintenance Issues
themes_detail.summary: Commercial disposal complaints spiked 700% two weeks ago (3 vs. 0.4 baseline, z-score: 3.77), while Maintenance/Facility complaints peaked 267% three weeks ago (28 vs. 7.6 baseline, z-score: 5.77), suggesting ongoing commercial space or building system failures.
evidence: Commercial disposal complaints: 3 filings 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 3.77)
Maintenance/Facility complaints: 28 filings 3 weeks ago vs. 7.6 weekly average (267% spike, z-score: 5.77)
Spike timing suggests acute episode triggered by seasonal weather, building system failure, or enforcement activity
reporting_angles: Map commercial disposal complaints to identify problem corridors or business clusters (restaurants, retail on Flatbush, Court Street, Seventh Ave)
Interview Sanitation Department about pickup schedules, commercial waste management regulations, and why this district spiked
Identify which buildings or facilities generated Maintenance complaints—likely NYCHA, city facilities, or large commercial properties
